payload.title: Measure the actual Frank v0.1 server-binary target VPS, token API and co-resident runtime contention
payload.work_clay: On the current Hostinger target VPS / digital-retina, capture an exact non-secret host identity and resource baseline, then execute matched service/runtime/API measurements representing the real v0.1 deployment. Record kernel/OS/arch, CPU topology/frequency/cgroup limits, RAM, swap, storage/filesystem/free-space and safe I/O characteristics, network/listener boundaries, accepted/current Frank binary+state identity where available, llama.cpp/model/mmproj identity, UnifiedDB/EAP placement and GitHub runner/service placement. Build or exercise the real server-binary communication path required by the owner directive: secure transport -> token auth -> request/session/provenance -> typed Frank ingress -> response/outcome receipt. Never expose raw production tokens; use secret injection and non-secret credential IDs/fingerprints in receipts. Measure valid/invalid/missing/revoked/rotated credential behavior, concurrency, timeout/cancellation, health/readiness, restart/recovery, provenance/session continuity, effectful idempotency/replay where applicable, and multimodal ingress when available. Measure cold/warm model load, prompt/decode throughput, Qwen3.5-4B abliterated Q4_K_M + mmproj fit when current artifacts are available, Retina visual encode path, EAP compile/end-to-end path, service startup/readiness, current-instance identity assertion/lease, stale-clone rejection and last-known-good restoration. Run a contention factorial: TARGET_IDLE, API_NO_MODEL, FRANK_QWEN_ONLY, FRANK_QWEN_PLUS_EAP, GITHUB_RUNNER_ONLY, FRANK_API_PLUS_RUNNER, and FRANK_API_PLUS_EAP_PLUS_RUNNER using bounded non-destructive workloads. Separate runtime/service/API effects from cross-repository runner transport. Use cgroup/systemd/affinity/priority isolation only as measured candidates, not assumptions.
payload.reason_clay: The project owner has changed v0.1 to a server-resident Frank identity on the Hostinger VPS and made the full token-authenticated API a release requirement. Existing evidence proves a real 4B Qwen-family model runs there on four logical CPUs, but exact RAM/swap/storage/GPU facts are not yet canonically captured and the same host also runs the GitHub Actions runner. There is also no observed final token-API acceptance receipt yet. Therefore target performance, memory fit, API overhead/security/recovery, binary-state self continuity and CI-vs-Frank interference are all release-critical unknowns rather than remote-lane details.
payload.completion_clay: A reproducible TARGET_VPS_RUNTIME_BASELINE_RECEIPT binds exact host/binary/state/runtime/model/API contract hashes and reports all observed host resources, server-binary startup/self-identity/recovery, Qwen3.5-4B+mmproj fit or exact blocker, p50/p95/p99 network-to-Frank response, prompt/decode/visual/EAP/end-to-end latency, CPU/RSS/swap/storage/network shadows and the matched co-residency contention matrix. In addition, FRANK_V0_1_TARGET_VPS_TOKEN_API_ACCEPTANCE_RECEIPT.json proves valid/invalid/missing/revoked/rotated credentials, concurrency, restart/readiness, request/session/provenance continuity, timeout/cancellation/errors, multimodal ingress if required, and idempotency/replay protections without exposing raw tokens. The report states whether the GitHub runner can coexist safely with interactive/API Frank load, whether isolation is required, and which resource envelope becomes the v0.1 acceptance baseline. Unknown hardware facts may become measured facts; no planned GPU/storage VPS values may be substituted. Disposition: TARGET_BASELINE_ESTABLISHED, REVISE_RESOURCE_ISOLATION, API_NOT_ACCEPTABLE, TARGET_HOST_BLOCKED, or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE.
controls: Frank API alone vs runner alone vs co-resident
frozen visual fixture vs live token-authenticated sensor API transport where available
no raw secret values in receipts
payload.executor_policy: This is final-target characterization and may run on the target VPS while BASE is in progress, but it must not destabilize active services. Prefer read-only host inspection and bounded benchmarks. Preserve service health before/after. API tokens must be injected through authorized secret/runtime mechanisms; raw production values never enter GitHub or normal logs. Do not launch paid training. Do not infer GPU/RAM/storage from planned hardware. If current target resources are insufficient, report the exact blocker and compare architecture/resource-isolation remedies before proposing a target-host change.
